name: One-pot cottage-cheese SALMON pasta (spelt) — protein-packed

source.author: Instagram — raz_yahav (Hebrew caption), salmon adaptation
source.notes: Canned-salmon version of onepot_cottage_tuna_spelt_pasta — salmon replaces the 3 tuna cans (~330 g drained). Removes the mercury flag and adds omega-3 + vitamin D + more calcium (esp. bone-in). Spelt pasta (user's usual). Cottage 5%, yellow cheese 9%. Big batch; servings assumed 6. The recommended version for the preconception lens.

ingredients.note: bone-in adds calcium + vitamin D; replaces the tuna
TASTE FIRST — cottage/cheese/salmon are already salty; likely needs much less

steps: Simmer spelt pasta + salmon + aromatics in the water in one wide pot until pasta is al dente and water absorbed; stir in cottage + yellow cheese off high heat until creamy.

batch_totals.note: Sodium ~9,100 mg batch (~1,520 mg/serving) — mostly the 1.5 tsp added salt on top of salty cottage/cheese/salmon. Cutting the added salt is the biggest lever.

him.verdict: The better version for your sperm goal. You give up ~3 g protein vs the tuna (49 vs 52 g/serving, still ~8 g/100 kcal) and gain ~3 g fat — but that fat brings ~770 mg omega-3 EPA/DHA AND ~275 IU vitamin D per serving (two sperm-priority micros the tuna barely had), plus more calcium. Same great cottage-cream protein + spelt fiber. The only shared problem is SODIUM (~1,520 mg/serving) from the added salt.
flags: VERY high sodium (~1,520 mg — the added salt)
suggested_mods: Skip or halve the added salt — biggest lever; cottage/cheese/salmon already bring plenty
Use bone-in canned salmon for the calcium + vitamin-D bump
Stir in spinach or peas at the end for folate/fiber

her_preconception.verdict: This swap turns the dish into a strong preconception meal: NO mercury flag (canned salmon is low-mercury), plus DHA (~770 mg omega-3, fetal brain development), vitamin D, and lots of calcium — on top of the protein. The only remaining knock is sodium; ease the added salt and it's excellent. This is the version to make for her.
prenatal_highlights: vitamin D (~275 IU) + high calcium (~436 mg)
high protein + spelt fiber; no mercury flag

safety_advisories.note: Very high sodium (~1,520 mg/serving) from the added salt — ease it in pregnancy.
safety_advisories.swap: skip/halve the added salt; taste first

suggested_mods: Make this instead of the tuna version — no mercury, more DHA + vitamin D
Bone-in canned salmon + a handful of spinach = calcium, vitamin D and folate in one dish

cooking_guide: For more depth, soften the sliced red onion + garlic in a little oil in the wide pot first (optional but worth it).
Add the dry spelt pasta, drained salmon (if bone-in, mash the soft bones in for extra calcium), pepper, chili and 2–2.5 cups water to the pot; bring to a simmer.

Cook uncovered, stirring often so the pasta doesn't stick, until the pasta is al dente and most of the water is absorbed (~10–12 min). Spelt can go from firm to soft quickly, so check early; add a splash more water if it dries before the pasta is done.
Lower the heat, then stir in the cottage cheese and grated yellow cheese until melted and creamy — keep it gentle (hard-boiling cottage can turn it grainy).
TASTE before adding the 1.5 tsp salt — the cottage, cheese and salmon are already salty, so you'll likely need much less or none. Biggest lever on the dish.
Rest 2–3 min off the heat to thicken; finish with fresh herbs and chili.
Tip: stir a couple of handfuls of spinach or some peas in at the end for folate + fiber.
